headline: Revenue and margin top guidance as dividend launches
summary_short: GlobalFoundries' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 6% y/y (9% q/q) to $1,786M, with Non-IFRS gross margin expanding 470bps y/y to 29.9% and beating the high end of guidance, while GAAP net income fell 27% y/y to $167M on higher SG&A and taxes even as GF paid its first-ever $0.12/share quarterly dividend.
summary_long: Revenue grew 6% y/y (9% q/q) to $1,786M on 7.6% higher wafer shipments and 21.1% Technology Services growth, partly offset by a 3.3% ASP decline. Non-IFRS gross margin rose 470bps y/y to 29.9%, above guidance, on favorable mix, lower D&A and better fixed-cost absorption. GAAP operating income fell 11% y/y as SG&A more than doubled (lower tool-sale gains, acquisition costs) and R&D rose 30% on the same acquisitions. Net income fell 27% y/y to $167M on higher tax expense, though Non-IFRS diluted EPS rose 10% y/y to $0.46. GF paid its first-ever dividend ($0.12/share) and declared a second for October. Q3 guidance: revenue $1,885M ±$25M, Non-IFRS diluted EPS $0.51 ±$0.05.

drivers.explanation: Grew 6% y/y (9% q/q) on 7.6% higher wafer shipment volumes (625k, 300mm-equivalent) and 21.1% Technology Services growth, partly offset by a 3.3% ASP decline reflecting demand patterns in certain end markets.

Non-IFRS gross margin rose 470bps y/y to 29.9%, beating the high end of guidance, on favorable product mix, lower depreciation/amortization and improved fixed-cost absorption, partly offset by lower customer underutilization payments.
Fell 11% y/y as SG&A more than doubled (+101%) on lower tool-sale gains and MIPS/Synopsys ARC Processor IP acquisition costs, while R&D rose 30% on the same acquisitions expanding headcount 61%.
Fell 27% y/y to $167M as income tax expense rose $36M on income in higher-tax jurisdictions, versus a $38M net tax benefit in the prior-year quarter.
Rose 10% y/y to $0.46 even as GAAP diluted EPS fell 27%, because non-IFRS excludes share-based compensation, acquisition-related amortization and one-off tax and revaluation items.

GF paid its first-ever quarterly dividend ($0.12/share, July 14) and declared a second for October 9; CEO Tim Breen cited "strong momentum, accelerating customer demand" in AI data-center optical networking.
